prerequisites: Knowledge of analog electronics is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to understand the different concepts linked to the accuracy of measurements and the characteristics of meters.
Ability to understand the characteristics of sensors and applications with particular attention to optoelectronic devices.
Be able to design conditioning circuits for passive sensors.
Be able to design conditioning circuits for signal-generating sensors.
Knowledge of the most common noise and interference reduction techniques and ability to design circuits to minimize their effects.
Ability to select and configure a data acquisition system as well as design basic systems.
Ability to incorporate signal processing techniques into instrumentation systems.
Ability to specify basic instrumentation systems.
Ability to synthesize and compare instrumentation systems.
Ability to select and compare common measurement instruments in the professional field.

syllabus_topics: Theory of measurement, errors, and calibration
teaching_methods: Expository classes (PowerPoint presentations and blackboard explanations)

assessment_methods.method: Evaluation of project work (design of an electronic instrumentation system)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, the final exam score must be 5 points or higher out of 10. The final score for the project work and practical assignments must be 5 points or higher out of 10. For students requesting differentiated evaluation, the written exam will account for 50% of the final grade and a project work (similar to that of other students) will account for the remaining 50%. Qualifications obtained are conserved exclusively for the calls of the same academic year.
